Incorporating the Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey around this period slightly brightens the near-term tone versus the FOMC statement alone. Banks reported easing standards and terms for C&I loans—especially to large and middle‑market firms—with firmer loan demand, aligning with strong business investment and supportive credit supply. Offsetting this, standards for certain CRE and consumer credit were tighter and demand softer, and the easing in C&I terms echoes the financial-stability concern about rising risk-taking (for example, in leveraged lending). Net: cyclical conditions remain firm and credit to businesses is accommodative, but medium‑term vulnerabilities persist. Overall, this nudges the assessment modestly more positive than the FSR‑tempered baseline.
